first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence suggests that reducing onboarding friction can improve time-to-value while activation messaging can strengthen first meaningful use. I would verify these two records before testing a focused onboarding simplification. A small guarded test should measure completion, activation, qualified pipeline or revenue, and retention so gains in early conversion do not mask lower downstream account quality. I am not prioritizing promotional pricing because it may defend SMB acquisition but is less aligned with sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

final.rationale: Run a standard guarded onboarding-simplification experiment this week. The current 4% onboarding decline is directly addressed, while verified evidence shows shortened onboarding improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%. This is the strongest sustainable-revenue option because it improves both near-term activation opportunity and downstream retention without discounting. Track onboarding completion, activation, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention; use activation messaging as a monitored secondary pathway rather than combining interventions in the single slot.
